findings.message: In 'automatic' mode, every_merges: 1 is still due after bb merges, because the mocked Retro commits no report and the window never resets. Serve's check_retro after bb therefore sets retro_due and runs a second forced=False retro at the next idle point. The final `assert calls == [False]` runs right after `terminals(rig, 'bb')` appears and races that second call. The mocked retro's own `assert not any(... bb ... running ...)` also fails on that second call, and run_retro re-raises it through serve. Whether the test passes depends on poll timing.
findings.paved_road: Make the outcome deterministic. Either have the automatic-mode mock journal what a committed report would, so the window resets, or wait until serve is idle after bb (no writers, a few polls elapsed) and assert the exact expected call list. Keep the bb-not-running assertion only for the first call.

findings.message: test_failed_retro_does_not_reblock cannot fail on the defect it is meant to rule out. The only point where a suppressed window could come due again is after bb settles, and the helper asserts `calls == [False]` as soon as bb reaches a terminal state, before serve's next loop could run a second retro. If the suppressing_failure check were removed from check_retro, serve would run the retro again (and block admission) after bb, but this assertion would usually still pass. Acceptance criterion 5 ('not run again for the same window') is therefore not demonstrated.
findings.paved_road: In 'failed' mode, after bb settles, wait until serve reaches an idle point (for example, until rig.owner.upgrade_idle() holds and several SERVE_POLL_S polls have passed). Then assert calls == [False] and that rig.owner.retro_pending() is False, so a re-blocking retro would make the test fail.
